html:
The Singing Revolution was the peaceful movement of 1987 to 1991 that restored the independence of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Its name comes from the mass singing at the Tallinn Song Festival Grounds.

Under Gorbachev's openness, protests began in 1987 over a plan for phosphate mining. In June 1988 crowds gathered night after night to sing banned national songs, and that September around 300,000 people, about a fifth of all Estonians, met at the Song Festival Grounds. The Baltic Way followed in 1989.

During the failed coup in Moscow, on 20 August 1991, Estonia declared its independence restored. The world recognised it within weeks. The movement drew on the tradition of the Song Festival, and on memory of the deportations.
sum: The Singing Revolution was the peaceful movement of 1987 to 1991 that restored the independence of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Its name comes from the mass singing at the Tallinn Song Festival Grounds.
